facts.value: keeps house for her uncle, Mr. Tobias Wray, at Holm Lodge
facts.quote: I keep house for my uncle, Mr. Tobias Wray, at Holm Lodge

facts.detail: on the table, laid there by Mr. Wray
facts.quote: he laid his gold repeater on the table in the garden room

facts.value: has two doors, one on the passage and one on the terrace, and no window that opens
facts.quote: The garden room has two doors and no window that opens

facts.detail: sewing in the window-seat, the passage door of the garden room in front of her
facts.quote: From four until the gong I sat sewing in the window-seat of the passage
It did not open once in those four hours

facts.detail: sitting by Ellen Wray, winding her wool
facts.quote: Philip sat by me, winding my wool, until the lamps were lit at dusk

facts.value: he will take a turn in the garden
facts.quote: he said he would take a turn in the garden

facts.detail: not seen again until the gong
facts.quote: I did not see him again until the gong

facts.detail: come in by the front door; talking with Ellen Wray
facts.quote: he stayed talking with me in the passage until eight
told me the rest on Sunday

facts.detail: clipping the yew, the terrace door of the garden room straight before him
facts.quote: I was clipping the yew on the terrace from four until dusk
It was shut the whole time

facts.detail: walking with his cigar, a dozen times past the terrace door
facts.quote: walked the terrace with his cigar until I put up my shears
At dusk I went home to my tea

facts.detail: pledged on Saturday night in Philip Wray's name
facts.quote: the watch was found at a pawnbroker's in Castle Street
